clue.text: Change tack if somewhat annoyed

definitions.meaning: to alter course in sailing, turning the vessel onto the other tack
British idiom for mildly upset or inconvenienced

explanation.definitionFit: In sailing the phrase means turning a ship onto a new heading; in British speech it also means bothered or inconvenienced.

clue.text: Homer needs George to enter his credit card code

indicators.note: to enter means to go inside, so the name is placed within the card code

parts.note: PIN is the personal identification number used with a card
GEO is a short form of the name George

explanation.surface: Homer Simpson asks a man named George to type in his card number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homer' looks like the poet or the cartoon father, but here it is a bird that flies home.
explanation.definitionFit: A homing bird used for racing and carrying messages is called a homer.

clue.text: Upset about local game

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards
about means surrounding, so the first word goes round the pub

parts.note: taken as written
a local is a British pub, an INN

explanation.surface: Someone is upset over a local game.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'Upset' into UP and SET: SET goes about INN to make SINNET, which 'Up' turns over in this down answer. A 'local' is a British neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket sport played over a net is a classic game.

clue.text: Start smiling-if you have money in American bonds!

definitions.meaning: cheer up, become happier

definitions.text: if you have money in American bonds!
definitions.meaning: bucks are dollars, so investors would want them to rise

explanation.definitionFit: To cheer up is to brighten, and dollars (bucks) going upward pleases American investors.

clue.text: One who promises to do a job with a grave purpose

definitions.text: One who promises to do a job with a grave purpose

parts.words: One who promises to do a job with a grave purpose
parts.note: someone who takes on a task; 'grave' means serious but also a burial place, pointing to a funeral director

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who agrees to a job undertakes it, and the funeral trade's worker deals with graves.

clue.text: What nervous people get when tempest 1is approaching gale force?

definitions.meaning: a state of jittery anxiety, a fit of the jitters
said of weather when the wind rises and strengthens

explanation.definitionFit: Anxious folk get the jitters in slang terms, and a strengthening storm has its breeze rising up.

clue.text: One takes Sunni movement on all at the same time

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: movement suggests the letters are moved around into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone joins a Sunni religious movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' looks like a religious movement but signals the anagram: SUNNI becomes NUNIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting together simultaneously means acting in concert, everyone together.

clue.text: Old Nick went first and worked as a printer's apprentice

parts.note: Old Nick is a nickname for the Devil
to go first is to lead, so LED

explanation.surface: Satan took the lead and then served as an errand boy in a print shop.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'printer's devil' was a print-shop errand boy or apprentice, so to devil is to do that work.
explanation.definitionFit: A printer's devil was the junior errand-runner in a print shop, so the verb means working in that role.

clue.text: Father's weapon used to gain entry

parts.note: PA is father, and the possessive gives PA'S
a sword is a bladed weapon

explanation.surface: Dad's blade was used to break in.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests forcing a way in with a blade, but the entry is gained with a secret word.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret word spoken or typed is how one gets admitted through a guarded door or login.

clue.text: General Officer Commanding orders "Die!"

parts.note: OC is the military abbreviation for Officer Commanding

indicators.note: orders here means arranges, so the letters of the following word are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A senior army commander barks a lethal command at his troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orders' looks like the commander's verb but signals the anagram: DIE becomes IDE. The whole clue also describes the mass killing a commander might command.
explanation.definitionFit: A general ordering death on a wide scale describes the deliberate extermination of a people.

clue.text: Fixes up about five graphic data lines

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the remedy word goes round the numeral

parts.note: to fix up an ailment is to cure it, giving CURES
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Someone repairs the plotted lines on a chart showing roughly five data points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'approximately five' but tells you CURES wraps round V.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines plotted on a graph to show data are called graphs' plotted bends, the usual term for such traced lines.

clue.text: Item of late news in the paper

definitions.text: Item of late news in the paper

parts.words: Item of late news in the paper
parts.note: 'late' suggests last-minute news but means deceased: a newspaper notice about someone who has died

explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's death notice reports on a person recently deceased, the 'late' person.

clue.text: Cause of feeling sick in the front of the ship?

definitions.text: Cause of feeling sick in the front of the ship?

indicators.note: in places the sickness word within the word for the ship's forward end

parts.note: the bow is the forward end of a vessel
to be feeling sick is to be ill

explanation.surface: A seasick passenger wonders what is upsetting their stomach at the prow.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a great swelling wave is what makes those at the bow feel queasy.
explanation.definitionFit: A large rolling sea wave is exactly what causes seasickness on board.

clue.text: What the camper did when laid low with malice aforethought

definitions.text: What the camper did when laid low
definitions.meaning: a camper who tumbled down would land inside the canvas shelter
fell means cruel or deadly, so a cruel intention, planned wickedness

explanation.definitionFit: A tumbling camper drops into the canvas, while 'fell' as an old word for cruel makes a cruel purpose or planned malice.

clue.text: Don't worry; there is a listener's refuge

parts.note: a haven is a safe refuge
a listener's thing is 'of ear', the ear being what listens

explanation.surface: A soothing voice reassures someone that there is a quiet place to be heard.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'a listener's refuge' as 'refuge of ear', then split the letters differently to get the reassuring phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling someone to be unafraid is a reassurance equivalent to telling them not to fret.

clue.text: Lose one's enthusiasm-for greenhouse cultivation?

definitions.meaning: to cool off, become less keen
greenhouses let plants be raised when the weather is chilly

explanation.definitionFit: Losing interest is cooling off, and greenhouses let gardeners raise plants in chilly weather.

clue.text: Tradesman who runs off to the South is a fast runner

parts.note: a tradesman who runs off copies is a printer

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper flees southwards, and proves very quick on his feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs off' sounds like fleeing but means producing copies on a press.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-distance racer who runs at top speed is a classic quick athlete.

clue.text: Take liberties to grant liberty

definitions.meaning: to behave too familiarly, presumptuously
to set someone loose, release them

explanation.definitionFit: Behaving presumptuously with something is making free with it, and releasing a slave was making them free.

clue.text: Somehow delay Peter time and time again

indicators.note: somehow suggests things done in some unspecified way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Peter is held up in some way, over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' signals an anagram of DELAY PETER.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something over and over is doing it frequently and recurrently.

clue.text: He runs after extra beer

definitions.meaning: a pursuer, someone giving chase
a drink taken after another, such as beer following a spirit

explanation.definitionFit: A pursuer gives chase, and a follow-up drink after a short of spirits has the same name.

clue.text: Take advantage of one male model

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to model is to pose for an artist

explanation.surface: Someone exploits a man who sits for artists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' is a noun on the surface but here the verb, to sit for an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit someone's good nature is to put upon them, a usage meaning take unfair advantage.

clue.text: Accent exacerbated by the modern hurly-burly

definitions.meaning: emphasis placed on a syllable
the mental strain worsened by hectic modern living

explanation.definitionFit: Emphasis on a syllable is the same word as the nervous strain that hectic modern life produces.

clue.text: One of the queue who gets a place in the restaurant

definitions.text: One of the queue who gets a place in the restaurant

parts.words: One of the queue who gets a place in the restaurant
parts.note: a person standing in line hoping for a table; but also the staff member who has a working place in a restaurant

explanation.definitionFit: Someone in a queue is one who waits, and a restaurant server also has that job title.

clue.text: Where a defeated wrestler must be hauled up

definitions.text: Where a defeated wrestler must be
definitions.meaning: pinned down on the floor covering of the ring
summoned to be reprimanded, in trouble with a superior

explanation.definitionFit: A beaten wrestler is pinned to the floor padding, and an employee being reprimanded is idiomatically in trouble before the boss.

clue.text: A tumultuous shout-of "How's that?"…

definitions.meaning: a loud clamour of protest
the cricket appeal to the umpire asking for a batsman to be given out

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, fielders shout 'How's that?' (often 'Howzat!') to ask the umpire to dismiss the batsman, so it is literally a cry of 'out'.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud public protest is a clamour, and the cricket appeal is a cry for a dismissal.

clue.text: … when only one batsman fails to get 200

definitions.text: when only one batsman fails to get
definitions.meaning: a cricket team has eleven batsmen; if one fails to score
a score is twenty, so ten of them make two hundred

explanation.walkthrough: A score is an old word for twenty. In cricket eleven players bat, so if only one fails to get a run, ten score.
explanation.definitionFit: Ten twenties make two hundred, and ten of eleven batsmen scoring fits the cricket reading.

clue.text: Strode hither and thither far from the madding crowd?

indicators.note: moving here and there in all directions suggests the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone strode back and forth, well away from the noisy throng.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hither and thither' signals an anagram of STRODE. Far from the Madding Crowd is Thomas Hardy's novel set in his fictional Wessex, based on this English county in southwest England.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardy's novel is set in the southwest English county his Wessex was modelled on.

clue.text: First course for course officials

definitions.meaning: the opening dishes of a meal
the people who start races at a racecourse

explanation.definitionFit: Appetisers open a meal, and at a racecourse the officials who send runners off bear the same name.
